Subject: Orbit AI renewal: capacity recalibration and safety pool proposal

Hi Marta —

Hope you had a good weekend. We pulled together the utilization windows from Q2 and early Q3 to shape a proposal for your upcoming renewal. Short summary up front: Orbit's 30‑day p50/p95 patterns show consistent growth in short burst windows tied to nightly retraining and a rising tail for live inference. That pattern suggests a small, permanent slab increase plus a modest safety pool (thermal/peak protection) rather than a straight tranche top‑up.

Key asks from our side: can you confirm whether the nightly retrain cadence will remain at 3x/week and whether the model family mix is shifting toward larger context lengths next quarter? That affects how many A100‑class equivalents we should reserve vs leave flexible.

Attached are: Orbit_Utilization_Report_Q2-2026.csv (raw telemetry), a draft SOW with two sizing options (permanent slab + safety pool vs short burst credits), and a thermal safety calculation sheet.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- You confirm retrain cadence + any planned model architecture changes (reply) — target 48 hours
- We run a trial policy for 2 weeks that routes non‑latency critical jobs into a burst lane to validate cost delta — Redwood action (Ben/Karthik)
- Post‑trial we finalize an amendment for renewal that maps to a committed slab + optional burst credits.

If that reads okay I can put Ben and Karthik on a 30‑minute call to walk through the sizing assumptions later today.

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — good summary. Quick answers:
- Retrain cadence stays at 3x/week for the next quarter (we have finance‑signoffs for now).
- We are planning a small architecture move: one model family will increase context windows from 4k to 8k in mid‑Sep, but inference QPS for that family should stay similar; memory pressure will increase.

Before we commit, procurement will need a clear delta on monthly committed cost and an outline of how the safety pool is consumed and replenished. Also can you confirm whether the safety pool has preemptible pricing or if it's charged at committed rates?

Ethan: can you join the call if needed — he'll want to see the SOW and the utilization slices.

Best,

Folks — forwarding Orbit's reply. Quick internal notes / asks before we jump on a call:

- Pricing mechanics: recommend we propose two lines on the SOW: 1) committed slab at a negotiated per‑GPU rate (guaranteed throughput), 2) safety pool implemented as burst credits priced at a discounted preemptible rate but with a minimum reclaim threshold. This preserves Orbit's predictability while giving them cheap headroom.

- Engineering validation: Karthik, can the runtime enforce a policy that routes 8k context jobs to nodes with higher memory allocation and keeps the 4k family on the standard pool? If yes, we can present a low‑risk migration plan to Orbit (non‑disruptive).

- Thermal/operational: Kimberly, the Thermal_Safety_Pool_Calc.xlsx shows a 12% headroom requirement to avoid hot‑standby spinups during nightly peaks — can you sanity check?

I suggest a 30‑minute call Wed 8/11 at 10am PT with Orbit — I'll draft a concise deck and revised SOW after we confirm engineering assumptions.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Orbit AI renewal: capacity recalibration and safety pool proposal

Hi all — happy to jump on Wed and wanted to surface the technical tradeoffs so the call is productive.

Summary of what we can deliver in short order: 
- Routing by model family/context length: yes — runtime can tag requests by model_id and context_length and route to a memory‑optimized slot pool. No code changes required, just a slot configuration and rollout (tested in staging).
- Safety pool behavior: we can implement a burst credit bucket that consumes at preemptible pricing (discounted) and automatically refills on a rolling monthly cadence. If Orbit prefers strict committed pricing for every consumed GPU minute, we can map credits to committed units instead; cost delta will be higher.
- Rollout plan (proposed): 1) 2‑week pilot that routes non‑critical batch retrains into burst lane (Ben configures); 2) monitor p95 latency and thermal metrics; 3) amend renewal with slab + burst credits if pilot validates.

I verified the thermal calc — Kimberly, the 12% headroom is conservative but acceptable for H100 clusters under Orbit's current mix. If they increase 8k context jobs significantly we should revisit with a slot memory reprofile.

Marta: if you confirm the retrain cadence and the 8k move (you already did) we can run the pilot starting Monday 8/16. I'll attach a short runbook post‑call.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
